| `align`, `lineHeight`                     | default paragraph style                                        |
| `meta`                                    | `{ title?, author? }`                                          |
| `fonts`                                   | custom fonts, see [Data & assets](/docs/react/data-and-assets) |
| `emoji`                                   | a color-emoji source, see [Emoji](/docs/pdf/emoji)             |

### Page

One page template. It lays its children out as a column, so `gap`, `justify` and `align` work here too.

| Prop               | Type                                                            |
| ------------------ | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `size`             | `"A4"`, `"Letter"`, ... or a custom size                        |
| `orientation`      | `"portrait"` \| `"landscape"`                                   |
| `margin`           | a number, or per-side insets                                    |
| `gap`              | space between children                                          |
| `justify`          | `"start"` \| `"center"` \| `"end"` \| `"between"` \| `"around"` |
| `align`            | `"start"` \| `"center"` \| `"end"` \| `"stretch"`               |
| `header`, `footer` | any element, repeated on every page                             |

`header` and `footer` are laid out once and repeated on every physical page the content flows onto,
with the space they need reserved - the content never runs under them:

```tsx
<Document>
  <Page
    size="A4"
    margin={48}
    header={
      <Text size={9} color="#94a3b8">
        ACME GmbH - Invoice
      </Text>
    }
    footer={
      <Row justify="between">
        <Text size={9} color="#94a3b8">
          acme.example
        </Text>
        <PageNumber size={9} color="#94a3b8" />
      </Row>
    }
  >
    <Text>... long content that paginates across pages ...</Text>
  </Page>
</Document>
```

## Layout

### Column and Row

Stack children vertically (`Column`) or horizontally (`Row`). Both take the options of the engine's
stacks: `gap`, `justify`, `align`, `wrap`, `reverse`, `alignContent`, a `width` and `height` in points
or `"%"`, and the page-break props below.

```tsx
<Row gap={12} justify="between" align="center">
  <Text bold>Item</Text>
  <Text>Value</Text>
</Row>
```

Every child can leave its line's alignment with `alignSelf`, move with `order` and take `minWidth`,
`maxWidth`, `minHeight`, `maxHeight` and `aspectRatio` - see [Layout](/docs/pdf/layout).

### Box

A sized, decorated container: background, border, padding, rounded corners.

| Prop                                                                       | Type                                 |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------ |
| `bg`                                                                       | a color, or a gradient               |
| `border`                                                                   | a color                              |
| `borderTop` / `borderRight` / `borderBottom` / `borderLeft`, `borderWidth` | per-side border control              |
| `padding`                                                                  | a number, or per-side insets         |
| `width`, `height`                                                          | points, or a percentage like `"50%"` |
| `radius`                                                                   | a number, or per-corner radii        |
| `relative`                                                                 | make it a positioning frame          |
| `overflow`                                                                 | `"hidden"` clips children to the box |

### Padding, Spacer, Expanded, Divider

- `<Padding insets={16}>` - wraps a child in space (a number or per-side insets).
- `<Spacer flex={1} />` - flexible empty space that pushes siblings apart.
- `<Expanded flex={1}>` - makes its child a flex item that takes its share of the remaining space;
  `flexBasis` and `flexShrink` as in CSS.
- `<Divider color="#e2e8f0" thickness={1} />` - a rule line.

## Text

### Text, Paragraph and Span

`Text` and `Paragraph` render their children as text; `Span` styles a run inside them. `Total: {sum}` is
one run, measured and kerned as one.

| Prop                                    | Type                                                         |
| --------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `size`, `font`, `color`                 | the basics; `font` also takes a fallback stack               |
| `bold`, `italic`                        | boolean shorthands                                           |
| `align`                                 | `"left"` \| `"center"` \| `"right"` \| `"justify"`           |
| `lineHeight`                            | line spacing multiplier                                      |
| `letterSpacing`, `wordSpacing`          | in points; negative tightens                                 |
| `textIndent`                            | first-line indent, in points                                 |
| `textTransform`                         | `"uppercase"` \| `"lowercase"` \| `"capitalize"` \| `"none"` |
| `underline`, `strikethrough`, `skipInk` | decoration; `skipInk` steps around descenders                |
| `direction`                             | `"ltr"` \| `"rtl"` - Hebrew and Arabic order correctly       |
| `ligatures`                             | `false` turns off `fi`/`fl`/`ffi`, which are on by default   |
| `breakWord`, `hyphenate`                | what to do with a word too long for its box                  |
| `orphans`, `widows`                     | minimum lines kept together at a page break                  |
| `maxLines`, `overflow`                  | `overflow` is `"clip"` \| `"ellipsis"`                       |
| `role`                                  | `"h1"`..`"h6"` \| `"p"` for a tagged, accessible PDF         |
| `href`                                  | link the text to an external URL                             |
| `to`                                    | link the text to an `<Anchor>`                               |

`<Span>` takes the run styles - `size`, `font`, `color`, `bold`, `italic`, the decorations,
`letterSpacing`, `wordSpacing`, `textTransform`, `ligatures`, `breakWord`, `hyphenate` - plus `href` /
`to` and `verticalAlign` (`"super"` \| `"sub"`), which shifts one run's baseline without resizing it.
What belongs to the whole paragraph stays on `<Text>`: `align`, `lineHeight`, `textIndent`,
`direction`, `maxLines`, `overflow`, `orphans`, `widows` and `role`.

```tsx
<Paragraph>
  Built with{" "}
  <Span href="https://jasy.dev" bold color="#1450aa">
    jasy
  </Span>
  , and this part is not a link.
</Paragraph>
```

Whitespace between spans is yours to write, as `{" "}` - JSX drops the line breaks around a tag.
`<DefaultTextStyle>` re-defaults the text style for a whole subtree, the per-section counterpart to the
`<Document>` defaults.

## Image

```tsx
<Image src={bytes} width={120} height={120} fit="cover" align="top" radius={8} alt="Logo" />
```

`src` takes image bytes (a `Uint8Array`), a URL, or - on the server - a path; see
[Data & assets](/docs/react/data-and-assets). `fit` is `"fill"` (the default), `"contain"`, `"cover"` or
`"none"`, and `align` says where the image sits in its box. Without a size the image is its own size,
scaled down to fit. The props are those of the [`Image` factory](/docs/pdf/images). An SVG source is
recognized by itself and stays a vector.

## Svg

```tsx
<Svg src={logoMarkup} width={120} alt="Acme" />
```

`src` takes SVG markup, the file's bytes, or - on the server - a path. With no size it draws at its
intrinsic size; pin one axis and the other follows the `viewBox`. `alt` makes it a `Figure` in a tagged
PDF. See [SVG and Canvas](/docs/pdf/drawing) for what the subset covers.

## Canvas

For a chart, a sparkline or a seal, `<Canvas>` hands your function a typed pen and the size the layout
resolved:

```tsx
import type { CanvasPaint } from "@jasy/pdf";

const months = [12, 19, 14, 27, 22, 31];

const sparkline: CanvasPaint = (c, { width, height }) => {
  const max = Math.max(...months);
  c.move(0, height - (months[0] / max) * height);
  months
    .slice(1)
    .forEach((v, i) =>
      c.line(((i + 1) / (months.length - 1)) * width, height - (v / max) * height),
    );
  c.stroke("#1450aa", { width: 1.5, cap: "round" });
};

<Canvas height={46} paint={sparkline} />;
```

The same function works at any width, so one definition serves a wide card and a narrow sidebar.

## Table

`<Table columns>` holds `<TableRow>`s of `<TableCell>`s. Mark a row `header` to repeat it on every page
the table flows onto. A number is a fixed width in points, `"1fr"` a flexible share, `"auto"` the widest
cell.

```tsx
<Table columns={["1fr", 120]} cellBorder="#e2e8f0" cellPadding={9}>
  <TableRow header>
    <TableCell>
      <Text bold>Description</Text>
    </TableCell>
    <TableCell>
      <Text bold>Amount</Text>
    </TableCell>
  </TableRow>
  {lines.map((line) => (
    <TableRow key={line.id}>
      <TableCell>{line.name}</TableCell>
      <TableCell>{`${line.total} EUR`}</TableCell>
    </TableRow>
  ))}
</Table>
```

A cell holds a string or any components. `Table` also takes `gap` / `rowGap` / `colGap`, `cellPadding`,
`cellBorder` and a `rule` color.

## Positioned

Out-of-flow placement, anchored to the nearest `<Box relative>` (or the page). Give it edges (`top` /
`right` / `bottom` / `left`) or an alignment (`h` / `v`) plus an `x` / `y` offset. `zIndex` sets the
paint order - see [Positioning](/docs/pdf/positioning).

```tsx
<Box relative height={200}>
  <Positioned top={8} right={8}>
    <Text size={9} color="#94a3b8">
      draft
    </Text>
  </Positioned>
</Box>
```

## Navigation

`<Link>` makes its child clickable. `href` opens a URL, `to` jumps to an `<Anchor>` in the same
document - exactly one of the two, and the types say so.

| Component    | Props                       |
| ------------ | --------------------------- |
| `<Link>`     | `href` \| `to`              |
| `<Anchor>`   | `name` (required)           |
| `<Bookmark>` | `title` (required), `level` |

A chapter heading usually wants a sidebar entry **and** a jump target. Nest them:

```tsx
<Bookmark title="2. Installation" level={1}>
  <Anchor name="install">
    <Text size={22} bold>
      2. Installation
    </Text>
  </Anchor>
</Bookmark>
```

See [Navigation](/docs/pdf/navigation) for how links, anchors and bookmarks work under the hood.

## Rotated and RotatedBox

`<Rotated angle>` spins its child at paint time: the layout box stays unrotated, so siblings do not
reflow - a stamp or a watermark. `<RotatedBox turns>` does layout-aware quarter-turns: a 90 or 270
degree turn swaps width and height, so a vertical label reserves exactly the strip it occupies.

```tsx
<Row gap={12}>
  <RotatedBox turns={3}>
    <Text bold>SECTION A</Text>
  </RotatedBox>
  <Rotated angle={-18}>
    <Box bg="#ffe9e9" border="#d33" padding={10}>
      <Text size={26} bold color="#d33">
        PAID
      </Text>
    </Box>
  </Rotated>
</Row>
```

## Page breaks

`<PageBreak />` cuts the flow: everything after it starts on a fresh page. `<KeepTogether>` refuses to
let its children be split and moves the whole group to the next page if it would not fit. Both also
exist as props (`breakBefore`, `breakAfter`, `keepTogether`) on `<Box>`, `<Column>` and `<Row>`.

```tsx
<Page>
  <Text size={18} bold>
    Terms
  </Text>
  <PageBreak />
  <Box keepTogether border="#d0d4da" radius={8} padding={14}>
    <Text bold>Signed</Text>
    <Text size={9}>This box is never torn across two pages.</Text>
  </Box>
</Page>
```

## Page numbers

`<PageNumber>` and `<PageCount>` print the current page and the document total; `<SubPageNumber>` and
`<SubPageCount>` count within one `<Page>`, for a document made of sections. They take the `<Text>`
props plus `offset`, which is added to the number (`-1` when a cover page should not count).

For anything else that depends on the page, `<PageBuilder>` takes a function as its child and builds
it for every page it lands on. Return `null` to show nothing on a page:

```tsx
<Page
  header={
    <PageBuilder>
      {({ pageNumber }) =>
        pageNumber === 1 ? null : <Text size={9}>Annual Report, continued</Text>
      }
    </PageBuilder>
  }
  footer={
    <PageBuilder>
      {({ pageNumber, pageCount }) => (
        <Text size={9} align="center">
          Page {pageNumber} of {pageCount}
        </Text>
      )}
    </PageBuilder>
  }
>
  {/* body */}
</Page>
```

The function receives `pageNumber`, `pageCount`, `pageSize`, `subPageNumber` and `subPageTotalPages`.
What it builds is placed whole on its page. Getting the total right is why jasy paginates the whole
document before it draws anything.

## Columns

`<SplitView>` sets its content in newspaper columns that continue on the next page and balance on the
last one. `<ColumnBreak />` starts the next column.

```tsx
<Page gap={12}>
  <Text size={28} bold color="#1450aa">
    The Valley Courier
  </Text>
  <SplitView columns={3} colGap={16} rowGap={8}>
    {paragraphs.map((p) => (
      <Text key={p.id}>{p.text}</Text>
    ))}
  </SplitView>
  <Text italic>This line follows the columns, right where they end.</Text>
</Page>
```

For a layout of your own, `<Flow>` takes it as the `page` render prop: one page of the layout, with a
`<Region />` wherever the content goes. It receives `{ index, pageNumber }`, so the first page can look
different from the rest.

```tsx
<Flow
  gap={8}
  page={({ index }) => (
    <Column gap={12}>
      {index === 0 ? (
        <Text size={22} bold color="#1450aa">
          Annual Report
        </Text>
      ) : (
        <Text size={9} italic>
          Annual Report, continued
        </Text>
      )}
      <Row gap={16}>
        <Expanded>
          <Region />
        </Expanded>
        <Box bg="#f3f5f9" padding={8}>
          <Region width={150} />
        </Box>
      </Row>
    </Column>
  )}
>
  {report.map((p) => (
    <Text key={p.id}>{p.text}</Text>
  ))}
</Flow>
```

`page` and a `PageBuilder`'s function are rendered in place, in your tree, while the PDF is laid out -
hooks and context work in them as anywhere else. The options, and the errors that name a mistake, are on
the [Columns](/docs/pdf/columns) page.

## Form fields

A form field is a layout element like any other: it reserves a box, flows with its neighbors, and emits
a widget the reader can type into. Seven kinds:

| Component        | For                                                             |
| ---------------- | --------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `TextField`      | one line or, with `multiline`, several; `password`, `maxLength` |
| `Checkbox`       | a single tick; `onValue` is what gets stored                    |
| `RadioGroup`     | one of several, laid out for you; `options` + `value`           |
| `Dropdown`       | a closed list, or `editable` to allow free text                 |
| `ListBox`        | a visible list; `multiSelect` for several at once               |
| `PushButton`     | an action - `"reset"`, `{ open: url }` or `{ submit: url }`     |
| `SignatureField` | an empty signature box for the reader to sign                   |

Every field takes `name` (the key the value is stored under), `required`, `hidden`, `print` and the
appearance props `border`, `background` and `color`. The single widgets add `tooltip`, `readOnly` and
`borderWidth`; the boxed ones (`TextField`, `Dropdown`, `ListBox`, `PushButton`, `SignatureField`) take
`width` and `height`, a `Checkbox` takes `size`. A `RadioGroup` is several buttons, so it has none of
those three: it takes `size`, `gap` and the label styling of its choices. The label of a `Checkbox`, a
`PushButton` or a `SignatureField` is its children:

```tsx
<Column gap={10}>
  <TextField name="fullName" width={220} height={22} border="#aab3c2" background="#fbfcfe" />
  <RadioGroup
    name="plan"
    gap={6}
    options={[
      { value: "basic", label: "Basic" },
      { value: "pro", label: "Pro" },
    ]}
  />
  <Dropdown name="country" width={110} height={22} options={["DE", "AT", "CH"]} />
  <Checkbox name="agree">I have read the statutes</Checkbox>
  <PushButton name="clear" action="reset" width={92} height={26}>
    Reset form
  </PushButton>
</Column>
```

There is no `onChange`: a generated PDF writes nothing back, so `value` is what the field starts with.
Reading a filled form back lives in the core: [Forms](/docs/pdf/forms).

## A component of your own

Your own components are React components - compose them from the set above, with props, hooks and
context:

```tsx
function Callout({ children }: { children: string }) {
  return (
    <Box bg="#eef1f5" border="#1450aa" radius={6} padding={12}>
      <Text color="#1450aa">{children}</Text>
    </Box>
  );
}
```

---

Source: https://jasy.dev/docs/react/data-and-assets
Summary: Drive the page with your data, and load custom fonts and images as bytes - in the browser or on a server.

# Data & assets

## Your data

A document is a component, so your data arrives as props. `map`, conditions, your own components,
context - anything that produces a tree produces a PDF.

```tsx
import { Divider, Document, Page, Row, Text } from "@jasy/react";

type Line = { id: number; name: string; price: number };

export function Statement({ lines }: { lines: Line[] }) {
  const total = lines.reduce((sum, l) => sum + l.price, 0);
  return (
    <Document size={11}>
      <Page size="A4" margin={48} gap={8}>
        {lines.map((line) => (
          <Row key={line.id} justify="between">
            <Text>{line.name}</Text>
            <Text>{line.price} EUR</Text>
          </Row>
        ))}
        <Divider />
        <Row justify="between">
          <Text bold>Total</Text>
          <Text bold>{total} EUR</Text>
        </Row>
      </Page>
    </Document>
  );
}
```

A PDF is rendered once, not kept alive like a page: load your data **before** `renderToPdf` and pass it
in. An effect that sets state after the first render (`useEffect` fetching data) comes too late - the
document has been read by then.

## Custom fonts

The standard PDF fonts (Helvetica, Times, Courier) need nothing. To use your own, register the font on
`<Document fonts>` under a name, then use that name as a `font`. In the browser, fetch the bytes first:

```tsx
const inter = new Uint8Array(await (await fetch("/fonts/Inter.woff2")).arrayBuffer());
const bytes = await renderToPdf(<Report font={inter} />);

function Report({ font }: { font: Uint8Array }) {
  return (
    <Document fonts={{ Inter: font }} font="Inter">
      <Page size="A4" margin={48}>
        <Text size={24} bold>
          Set in Inter
        </Text>
      </Page>
    </Document>
  );
}
```

The container does not matter: **`.ttf`, `.woff` and `.woff2` are the same thing here** - jasy unwraps
the wrapper itself. The font is subsetted on the way into the PDF, so the file stays small. For weights,
register one file per style: `fonts={{ Inter: { normal, bold, italic } }}`.

On a **server** a plain path works too - `fonts={{ Inter: "./fonts/Inter.woff2" }}` is the whole story.
In the browser there is no filesystem to point at, so it is bytes.

## Images

`<Image src>` takes the image bytes as a `Uint8Array`, a URL, or - on a server - a path. JPEG and PNG
both work, and PNG transparency composites over whatever sits behind it, not a white box.

```tsx
const logo = new Uint8Array(await (await fetch("/logo.png")).arrayBuffer());

<Image src={logo} width={120} height={40} fit="contain" />;
```

A URL is fetched while the document is prepared, before the layout runs, so its size is known when the
page is laid out.

## Render options

`renderToPdf` (and `renderToPdfString`) take the engine's render options as their second argument:

```tsx
const bytes = await renderToPdf(<Invoice {...data} />, {
  onOverflow: "warn",
  accessible: true,
  encrypt: { userPassword: "secret" },
  onDiagnostic: (d) => console.log(d.code, d.message),
});
```

- `onOverflow` - what happens when a single unbreakable element is taller than the page: `"error"`
  (default) throws, `"warn"` places it clipped and logs, `"ignore"` places it clipped.
- `accessible` - a tagged PDF with a structure tree for screen readers, see
  [Accessibility](/docs/pdf/accessibility).
- `encrypt` - AES-256 password protection, see [Encryption](/docs/pdf/encryption).
- `onDiagnostic` - everything the engine has to say about the document, one call per finding, see
  [Output](/docs/pdf/output).

## A descriptor for a server

`toDocumentDescriptor(element)` stops before the PDF and returns the engine's descriptor: a plain
`{ type, props, children }` tree. To post it as JSON, encode font and image bytes yourself - JSON has no
`Uint8Array` - and decode them on the other side. Functions do not survive JSON at all, so a document
with a `Canvas`, a `Flow` or a `PageBuilder` goes through `renderToPdf`.

---

Source: https://jasy.dev/docs/invoicing
Summary: Generate conformant ZUGFeRD and XRechnung e-invoices in Node.js - the PDF/A-3 and the EN-16931 XML - from one typed object, checked with the KoSIT rules and veraPDF.

# E-invoices

A ZUGFeRD or XRechnung invoice is a normal-looking PDF that **also** carries the invoice as
machine-readable XML inside it. The human reads the PDF; the buyer's system reads the embedded EN-16931
data. Germany now mandates this for B2B and B2G, and the rest of the EU is moving the same way.

`@jasy/e-invoice` builds both halves from a single typed `Invoice`: a conformant PDF/A-3 with the
EN-16931 CII XML embedded, with every total and VAT line **computed for you**. No Java, no service, no
spreadsheet math.

> The other ecosystems have Mustangproject (Java), horstoeko/zugferd (PHP) and factur-x (Python). Node
> had nothing polished. This is it.

## Install

```bash
pnpm add @jasy/e-invoice
```

It pulls in `@jasy/pdf` itself, so that is the only package you need.

## At a glance

You describe the invoice as one typed object; `renderZugferd` hands back both halves. You never add up
a line, a subtotal or a VAT breakdown.

```ts
const { bytes, xml } = await renderZugferd(invoice);
// bytes - a conformant ZUGFeRD PDF/A-3, with the EN-16931 XML embedded
// xml   - the same EN-16931 CII, standalone for a portal upload
```

That is the whole shape of it. For an invoice you can paste and run end to end, jump to
[A complete example](/docs/invoicing/complete-example).

## What you get

- A **PDF/A-3** with the `factur-x.xml` embedded, a Factur-X XMP packet and an sRGB output intent -
  the structure conformance checkers expect.
- The **EN-16931 CII XML**, the legally relevant part, also returned standalone for portal upload.
- **Totals by construction:** line nets, the document totals and the VAT breakdown are derived from
  your inputs, so the business-rule checks that verify the arithmetic hold automatically.

## Where to next

- [**The Invoice model**](/docs/invoicing/invoice-model) - every field you can set, parties to VAT.
- [**Profiles**](/docs/invoicing/profiles) - ZUGFeRD (EN-16931) vs XRechnung, and CII vs UBL.
- [**Your own layout**](/docs/invoicing/appearance) - the language, the labels, or a page you designed yourself.
- [**Validation**](/docs/invoicing/validation) - the built-in pre-flight, and validating it yourself.
- [**A complete example**](/docs/invoicing/complete-example) - the fields at a glance, a full sample, the CLI proof.
- [**The CLI**](/docs/cli) - read, validate and export any invoice from your terminal.

---

Source: https://jasy.dev/docs/invoicing/invoice-model
Summary: Every field you can set on an Invoice - from the handful you need to the full EN-16931 detail. Parties, lines, VAT, payment and more.

# The Invoice model

Afraid of the official paperwork? Don't be. EN-16931 defines a long list of fields, but **you need a
handful.** Fill in the few that are mandatory, add detail only where your case calls for it, and the
library computes every total and writes the conformant XML underneath. Each field maps to a real
business term (its `BT-` / `BG-` code lives in the type, for when you ever need it).

## The smallest invoice

This is already a complete, conformant invoice. Everything else on this page is optional.

```ts
import { type Invoice } from "@jasy/e-invoice";

const invoice: Invoice = {
  number: "INV-001",
  issueDate: "2026-06-21", // ISO date
  currency: "EUR",
  seller: {
    name: "Northwind GmbH",
    vatId: "DE265013614",
    address: { city: "Berlin", postCode: "10115", country: "DE" },
  },
  buyer: {
    name: "Globex Ltd",
    address: { city: "Munich", postCode: "80331", country: "DE" },
  },
  lines: [
    {
      name: "Consulting",
      quantity: 8,
      unit: "HUR",
      netUnitPrice: 120,
      vat: { category: "S", ratePercent: 19 },
    },
  ],
};
```

`number`, `issueDate`, `currency`, `seller`, `buyer` and at least one line - that is the whole
requirement. Hand it to [`renderZugferd`](/docs/invoicing) and out come the PDF and the XML.

## Seller and buyer

Both parties take the same shape. A **name** and an **address** (only the `country` is required) are
mandatory; everything else is opt-in.

```ts
seller: {
  name: "Northwind GmbH", // registered legal name
  vatId: "DE265013614", // needed whenever you charge VAT
  address: { line1: "Hauptstrasse 1", city: "Berlin", postCode: "10115", country: "DE" },
  contact: { name: "A. Schmidt", email: "billing@northwind.de", phone: "+49 30 123456" },
  electronicAddress: "billing@northwind.de", // required for XRechnung / Peppol
},
```

Other handy fields: `tradingName`, `taxNumber` (Steuernummer), `legalRegistrationId`
(Handelsregisternummer) and `additionalLegalInfo` (BT-33, the legal footer line - share capital,
managing director). The `buyer` mirrors all of it.

The address takes more than the four above when you need them: `line2` and `line3` for a second and
third street line, and `subdivision` for a region, county or state (BT-39 / BT-54). Only `country` is
mandatory.

## Lines

Each line names an item, a quantity in a unit, the net unit price and its VAT. The library multiplies
and sums - you never add up a line yourself.

```ts
lines: [
  {
    name: "Consulting",
    description: "On-site workshop", // optional
    quantity: 8,
    unit: "HUR", // UN/ECE Rec 20 - "HUR" hours, "C62" pieces, "DAY", "KGM" kg, "MTR" meter ...
    netUnitPrice: 120,
    vat: { category: "S", ratePercent: 19 },
  },
  {
    name: "License",
    quantity: 1,
    unit: "C62",
    netUnitPrice: 480,
    vat: { category: "S", ratePercent: 19 },
  },
],
```

More per line when you need it: `sellerItemId` / `buyerItemId` / `standardItemId` (a GTIN),
`priceBaseQuantity` (a price "per 100"), per-line `allowancesCharges`, and a free-text `note`.

And, for the customers who reconcile automatically:

```ts
{
  name: "Meter type M-200",
  quantity: 2,
  unit: "C62",
  netUnitPrice: 480,
  vat: { category: "S", ratePercent: 19 },
  orderLineRef: "12",            // which line of their order this settles (BT-132)
  objectRef: "METER-99213",      // the thing being invoiced (BT-128)
  buyerAccountingRef: "CC-4712", // their cost center, for this line (BT-133)
  originCountry: "CH",           // country of origin (BT-159)
}
```

## VAT

VAT sits **on the line** (and on any allowance or charge): a category plus its rate.

| Category | Meaning                     | Rate                   |
| -------- | --------------------------- | ---------------------- |
| `S`      | Standard rate               | the percent, e.g. `19` |
| `Z`      | Zero-rated                  | `0`                    |
| `E`      | Exempt from VAT             | omit                   |
| `AE`     | Reverse charge              | omit                   |
| `K`      | Intra-community supply (EU) | omit                   |
| `G`      | Export outside the EU       | omit                   |
| `O`      | Outside the scope of VAT    | omit                   |

For the non-standard categories EN-16931 wants a **reason**. Give it once per category:

```ts
const invoice: Invoice = {
  // ... every line uses { category: "AE" } ...
  vatExemptionReasons: {
    AE: {
      text: "Reverse charge - Steuerschuldnerschaft des Leistungsempfängers (§13b UStG)",
      code: "VATEX-EU-AE",
    },
  },
};
```

## The optional extras

Reach for these as your case calls for them. None are required.

**Dates and references**

```ts
dueDate: "2026-07-05",
buyerReference: "04011000-12345-34", // the Leitweg-ID - MANDATORY for XRechnung (B2G)
purchaseOrderRef: "PO-7782",   // their order number (BT-13)
salesOrderRef: "SO-1190",      // yours (BT-14)
contractRef: "C-2026-09",
projectRef: "New hall 4",      // project the invoice belongs to (BT-11)
tenderRef: "VgV-2026-0031",    // tender or lot, for public procurement (BT-17)
objectRef: "METER-99213",      // what is being invoiced, when it is a thing (BT-18)
buyerAccountingRef: "CC-4711", // their cost center (BT-19)
notes: ["Thank you for your business."],
noteSubjectCode: "AAI",        // what the notes are about, coded (BT-21)
```

Large customers often insist on `buyerAccountingRef`: it is what lets their accounting route the
invoice without a person reading it. Both parties can also carry a directory identifier - a GLN or
similar - as `seller.identifier` (BT-29) and `buyer.identifier` (BT-46).

**Payment** - so the buyer knows where and how to pay:

```ts
payment: {
  meansCode: "58", // SEPA credit transfer (UNCL 4461); "30" is a plain credit transfer
  iban: "DE89370400440532013000",
  bic: "COBADEFFXXX",
  accountName: "Northwind GmbH",
  terms: "Payable within 14 days, net.",
  reference: "RE-2026-0184", // BT-83, what the payer should quote; defaults to the invoice number
  meansText: "SEPA direct debit", // BT-82, when a code alone does not say it
},
```

`reference` is the remittance information - the string the payer puts on the transfer. Leave it out
and the invoice number is used, which is what you want almost always.

### Skonto - an early-payment discount

"2% within 14 days" is **not** a discount in EN-16931 sense, and this is the one place where the
obvious workaround produces a wrong invoice. A discount that only applies if the buyer pays early
must not reduce the invoice total, because at the time of issue nobody knows whether it will be
taken. So it lives in the payment terms:

```ts
payment: {
  iban: "DE89370400440532013000",
  terms: "Payable within 30 days.",
  cashDiscounts: [
    { days: 14, percent: 2 },  // 2% if paid within 14 days
    { days: 30, percent: 1 },
  ],
},
```

The base is the invoice total including VAT, which is what German practice calculates Skonto on;
override it per tier with `baseAmount`. The totals do not move - the discount is printed on the page
and written into BT-20 in the machine-readable form XRechnung prescribes:

```
#SKONTO#TAGE=14#PROZENT=2.00#
```

::callout{type="warning"}
Do not model Skonto as an `allowancesCharges` entry. The amount would be deducted immediately
although it is only due on early payment - a file that passes every validator and states the wrong
sum. `xrechnungProblems()` looks for exactly that mistake and names it.
::

### SEPA direct debit

When you collect rather than being paid, the payer needs to recognize the debit on their statement:

```ts
payment: {
  meansCode: "59", // SEPA direct debit (UNCL 4461); "58" is a SEPA credit transfer
  directDebit: {
    mandateReference: "MND-2024-00871", // the mandate they signed (BT-89)
    creditorId: "DE98ZZZ09999999999",   // your creditor identifier (BT-90)
    debitedIban: "DE02120300000000202051", // the account to be debited (BT-91)
  },
},
```

All three go on the page as well as into the XML. A collection with no mandate reference is
reported by the pre-flight, because the payer cannot check it against anything.

**Document-level discounts or charges** - applied after the line sum, each with its own VAT:

```ts
allowancesCharges: [
  { isCharge: false, amount: 50, reason: "Loyalty discount", vat: { category: "S", ratePercent: 19 } },
  { isCharge: true, amount: 12, reason: "Shipping", vat: { category: "S", ratePercent: 19 } },
],
```

Each also takes a `reasonCode` - the coded counterpart of `reason` (UNCL 5189 for an allowance, UNCL
7161 for a charge). Some receivers match on the code rather than the text.

You can state a **percentage** instead of a fixed sum, and then "10%" survives into the XML and onto
the page rather than being silently converted to euros:

```ts
allowancesCharges: [
  {
    isCharge: false,
    baseAmount: 3980, // what the percentage applies to (BT-93)
    percent: 10,      // the rate (BT-94)
    reason: "Framework agreement",
    vat: { category: "S", ratePercent: 19 },
  },
],
```

The amount is derived. It works the same way on a line (BT-137/138 and BT-142/143). Give an explicit
`amount` **and** a percentage and the amount wins - overruling you would hide a typo - but the
pre-flight reports the disagreement with both figures.

The page then reads `Framework agreement (10% of €3,980.00) -€398.00` instead of an unexplained
`-€398.00`.

## Credit notes and corrections

A credit note that does not say what it corrects cannot be matched to its original, and the original
is what an auditor searches for:

```ts
const creditNote: Invoice = {
  number: "CN-2026-0011",
  type: 381, // credit note
  precedingInvoices: [{ number: "INV-2026-0187", issueDate: "2026-08-14" }],
  // ... the rest as usual
};
```

Several are allowed - one correction may settle more than one invoice. The date is optional but is
what disambiguates a number that repeats across years.

## Attachments

A timesheet, a proof of service, a delivery note. Anyone billing by effort has one, and sending it
separately by e-mail loses exactly the advantage e-invoicing exists for:

```ts
supportingDocuments: [
  {
    reference: "TIMESHEET-09",
    description: "Timesheet September",
    file: {
      content: readFileSync("timesheet.csv"), // Uint8Array
      mimeType: "text/csv",
      filename: "timesheet.csv",
    },
  },
  // or a link instead of a file:
  { reference: "AB-2026-14", description: "Order confirmation", url: "https://…/ab.pdf" },
],
```

A `file` travels **twice**: base64 inside the XML where a machine finds it, and as an embedded file
in the PDF/A-3 where a person double-clicks it. Only the invoice XML is marked as the invoice data;
attachments are marked as supplements. The page names them, so nobody has to think to look in the
attachment pane.

**And a few more:** `delivery` (`date`, `recipientName`, a deliver-to `address`, and `locationId` for
a site number instead of an address), `payeeName` with `payeeIdentifier` and
`payeeLegalRegistrationId` (when payment goes to someone other than the seller - a factor, say),
`paidAmount` (already paid, subtracted to give the amount due) and `type` (`380` a commercial
invoice, `381` a credit note).

## Rounding to a clean payable

Some houses collect a round figure. `roundingAmount` is a signed number **added to the amount due**;
the invoice total itself does not move:

```ts
roundingAmount: -0.4, // 107.40 total -> 107.00 payable
```

The page prints the rounding line with its sign, because a payable that does not equal the total
minus what was paid otherwise looks like an arithmetic error.

## Invoicing in a foreign currency

If the invoice is not in euros, a German seller still owes the tax office the VAT figure in euros.
Say so, or the invoice is legally deficient:

```ts
currency: "USD",
taxCurrency: "EUR",          // the currency VAT is accounted in (BT-6)
taxTotalInTaxCurrency: 172.4, // the VAT total in it (BT-111)
```

::callout{type="info"}
The conversion is **yours**, not ours. Which exchange rate applies - the supply date, the invoice
date, the monthly average - is a tax question, and putting a number on an invoice that nobody chose
would be worse than asking for it. `xrechnungProblems()` warns whenever the currency is not EUR and
no accounting currency is given.
::

That is the whole model. Start from the smallest invoice and add only what you need - the totals and
the XML stay correct underneath, every time.

---

Source: https://jasy.dev/docs/invoicing/profiles
Summary: Two small choices with sensible defaults - ZUGFeRD or XRechnung, and the CII or UBL XML syntax.

# Profiles

Two small decisions, both with a default you rarely change: **which conformance profile** (ZUGFeRD or
XRechnung) and **which XML syntax** (CII or UBL). The same `Invoice` feeds all of them - you just pick.

## ZUGFeRD or XRechnung?

```ts
renderZugferd(invoice); // ZUGFeRD (en16931) - the default
renderZugferd(invoice, { profile: "xrechnung" }); // German B2G
```

**ZUGFeRD (`en16931`)** is the default and what most invoices want: standard EN-16931, works for B2B
across Europe. Nothing to set.

**XRechnung (`xrechnung`)** is for selling to a German public authority (B2G), where it is mandatory.
It is EN-16931 plus stricter German rules - a few extra fields are required:

- the **Leitweg-ID** in `buyerReference` (the authority gives you this),
- an **electronic address** on both the seller and the buyer,
- a full **seller contact** (name, phone, email) and city + post code,
- a **due date** or payment **terms**, and an **IBAN** for a credit transfer.

Here is the reassuring part: you do not have to memorize that list. Choose the profile and the library
**pre-checks** it, throwing one clear, field-named error if anything is missing - long before a portal
ever rejects it.

```ts
// Missing the Leitweg-ID? You get told exactly that, with the field to set:
// Error: Invoice is not XRechnung-ready:
//   - XRechnung needs the Leitweg-ID - set invoice.buyerReference (BT-10).
await renderZugferd(invoice, { profile: "xrechnung" });
```

The extra fields a complete XRechnung needs, in one place:

```ts
const invoice: Invoice = {
  // ... the usual fields ...
  buyerReference: "04011000-12345-34", // Leitweg-ID (BT-10)
  dueDate: "2026-07-05",
  seller: {
    name: "Northwind GmbH",
    vatId: "DE265013614",
    electronicAddress: "billing@northwind.de", // BT-34
    contact: { name: "A. Schmidt", phone: "+49 30 123456", email: "billing@northwind.de" },
    address: { line1: "Hauptstrasse 1", city: "Berlin", postCode: "10115", country: "DE" },
  },
  buyer: {
    name: "Bundesamt fuer Beschaffung",
    electronicAddress: "einkauf@behoerde.de", // BT-49
    address: { city: "Bonn", postCode: "53113", country: "DE" },
  },
  payment: { iban: "DE89370400440532013000", terms: "Payable within 30 days." },
  // ... lines ...
};
```

You can also run the check yourself, without rendering, to gate a form or a save button:

```ts
import { xrechnungProblems } from "@jasy/e-invoice";

const problems = xrechnungProblems(invoice); // string[] - empty means good to go
```

## CII or UBL?

EN-16931 has two interchangeable XML syntaxes. You almost never have to think about this.

**CII** (Cross Industry Invoice) is the ZUGFeRD / Factur-X standard, and it is what `renderZugferd`
embeds and returns in `.xml`. That is the default and what you want.

```ts
const { bytes, xml } = await renderZugferd(invoice); // xml is the CII
```

Need the XML **on its own** - say, a portal that wants a file upload - or specifically **UBL**
(Universal Business Language, the other EN-16931 syntax some systems prefer)? Compute once, then
convert:

```ts
import { computeInvoice, toCII, toUBL } from "@jasy/e-invoice";

const computed = computeInvoice(invoice);
const cii = toCII(invoice, computed); // same XML renderZugferd embeds
const ubl = toUBL(invoice, computed, "xrechnung"); // UBL, XRechnung CIUS
```

Both accept the profile (`"en16931"` default, or `"xrechnung"`), so the guideline identifier inside the
XML matches what you are filing.

---

Source: https://jasy.dev/docs/invoicing/validation
Summary: Three layers of confidence - totals correct by construction, a build-time pre-flight, and the finished file validated against the official rules, on your own machine.

# Validation

Confidence comes in three layers, each stronger than the last: the math is right by construction, a
pre-flight catches missing fields before you render, and you can validate the finished file against the
exact rules the authorities use - on your own machine, with nothing leaving it.

## The totals can't be wrong

You never type a subtotal. The library derives every line net, the document totals and the VAT
breakdown from your quantities and prices, so the EN-16931 arithmetic rules (the `BR-CO-*` checks that
the sums add up) hold automatically. The one error that trips most invoices - a total that does not
match its lines - simply cannot happen here.

## The pre-flight, before you render

When you target XRechnung, the library checks the mandatory B2G fields and tells you, by field name,
what is missing - at build time, in your editor:

```ts
import { xrechnungProblems, en16931Problems } from "@jasy/e-invoice";

const problems = xrechnungProblems(invoice); // string[]; empty means good to go
if (problems.length) console.error(problems.join("\n"));
```

There are two checks, for the two profiles. `en16931Problems` covers what **every** EN-16931 invoice
needs; `xrechnungProblems` adds what the German B2G rules want on top - the Leitweg-ID above all.
Each returns plain sentences you can show a user, not rule codes:

```
XRechnung needs the Leitweg-ID - set invoice.buyerReference (BT-10).
```

`renderZugferd(invoice, { profile: "xrechnung" })` runs the same check and throws if anything is
missing, so a missing Leitweg-ID surfaces as a clear error now, not as a cryptic portal rejection weeks
later. (See [Profiles](/docs/invoicing/profiles).)

## Verify the finished file - yourself

Here is the part that should put any doubt to rest: **don't take our word for it.** The `@jasy/cli`
validates any ZUGFeRD or XRechnung PDF against the **official KoSIT Schematron rules** - the very same
ones the German authorities run - plus the EN-16931 business rules, entirely **on your machine**.
Nothing is uploaded.

```bash
npx @jasy/cli validate ./invoice.pdf
```

It reports the EN-16931 rules and the PDF/A-3 structure, and `jasy verapdf` adds the full ISO PDF/A
check via [veraPDF](https://verapdf.org), the official open-source validator. The file you generated
passes the same gates a tax office puts it through - and you watched it happen, locally.

See [**The CLI**](/docs/cli) for reading, validating and exporting any invoice from your terminal.

---

Source: https://jasy.dev/docs/invoicing/complete-example
Summary: Everything in one place - the fields at a glance, a full invoice you can paste and run, and the proof that it validates.

# A complete example

Everything from the last pages, together: the fields at a glance, a complete invoice you can paste and
run, and the proof that the file it produces is valid - checked on your own machine. Afraid this is
complicated? Watch how short it is.

## The fields at a glance

You need the essentials. Everything else you add only if your case calls for it.

**Always**

| Field                                                                      | Needed?                  |
| -------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------ |
| `number`, `issueDate`, `currency`                                          | Yes                      |
| `seller` - `name` + `address` (country)                                    | Yes                      |
| `buyer` - `name` + `address` (country)                                     | Yes                      |
| `lines` - at least one (`name`, `quantity`, `unit`, `netUnitPrice`, `vat`) | Yes                      |
| `seller.vatId`                                                             | Yes, when you charge VAT |

**Optional - reach for these as needed**

| Field                                         | What it adds                    |
| --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- |
| `dueDate`, `payment` (IBAN, terms)            | payment details                 |
| `notes`, `purchaseOrderRef`, `contractRef`    | references                      |
| `allowancesCharges`                           | document discounts / surcharges |
| `paidAmount`, `payeeName`, `delivery`, `type` | the long tail                   |

**XRechnung (German B2G) additionally requires**

| Field                                      | What it is            |
| ------------------------------------------ | --------------------- |
| `buyerReference`                           | the Leitweg-ID        |
| `seller` / `buyer` `.electronicAddress`    | electronic addresses  |
| `seller.contact` (name, phone, email)      | a reachable contact   |
| `dueDate` or `payment.terms`, plus an IBAN | due date + how to pay |

If an XRechnung is missing any of these, the library tells you by field name - see
[Validation](/docs/invoicing/validation).

## A complete invoice

Paste this into `invoice.ts`, run `npx tsx invoice.ts`, and you get `invoice.pdf` and `invoice.xml`.

```ts
import { writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { renderZugferd, type Invoice } from "@jasy/e-invoice";

const invoice: Invoice = {
  number: "INV-001",
  issueDate: "2026-06-21",
  currency: "EUR",
  dueDate: "2026-07-05",
  purchaseOrderRef: "PO-7782",
  notes: ["Thank you for your business."],
  seller: {
    name: "Northwind GmbH",
    vatId: "DE265013614",
    address: { line1: "Hauptstrasse 1", city: "Berlin", postCode: "10115", country: "DE" },
    contact: { name: "A. Schmidt", email: "billing@northwind.de", phone: "+49 30 123456" },
  },
  buyer: {
    name: "Globex Ltd",
    address: { line1: "5 Market Square", city: "Munich", postCode: "80331", country: "DE" },
  },
  lines: [
    {
      name: "Consulting",
      description: "On-site workshop",
      quantity: 8,
      unit: "HUR",
      netUnitPrice: 120,
      vat: { category: "S", ratePercent: 19 },
    },
    {
      name: "License",
      quantity: 1,
      unit: "C62",
      netUnitPrice: 480,
      vat: { category: "S", ratePercent: 19 },
    },
  ],
  allowancesCharges: [
    {
      isCharge: false,
      amount: 50,
      reason: "Loyalty discount",
      vat: { category: "S", ratePercent: 19 },
    },
    { isCharge: true, amount: 12, reason: "Shipping", vat: { category: "S", ratePercent: 19 } },
  ],
  payment: {
    iban: "DE89370400440532013000",
    bic: "COBADEFFXXX",
    accountName: "Northwind GmbH",
    terms: "Payable within 14 days, net.",
  },
};

async function build() {
  const { bytes, xml } = await renderZugferd(invoice, { locale: "en" });
  writeFileSync("invoice.pdf", bytes); // the ZUGFeRD PDF/A-3
  writeFileSync("invoice.xml", xml); // the EN-16931 CII XML
}

build();
```

Every total is worked out for you: the net (1402.00), the 19% VAT (266.38) and the gross (1668.38)
come from the lines, the discount and the surcharge - you never add them up.

## Validate it

Now prove it. Nothing is uploaded - it runs on your machine:

```bash
npx @jasy/cli validate ./invoice.pdf
```

```text
  invoice.pdf  ·  ZUGFeRD · EN 16931 (CII)

  EN 16931 rules      ✓ valid
  PDF/A-3 structure   ✓ 13/13
  PDF/A (veraPDF)     ✓ compliant

  → VALID
```

That is the whole loop: you described the invoice, the library built the PDF and the XML and did the
math, and the same checker a tax office uses confirmed it - on your machine. Create, validate, done.

---

Source: https://jasy.dev/docs/invoicing/appearance
Summary: Change the language and the labels of the built-in invoice, or hand renderZugferd a document you designed yourself - the XML stays conformant either way.

# Your own layout

A ZUGFeRD file is two things in one: a **PDF a person reads** and an **XML a machine reads**. Only the
XML has to satisfy EN 16931. The page is yours.

jasy keeps those apart, so you can restyle the invoice as far as you like without ever risking
conformance - the XML is derived from the same `Invoice` object no matter what the page looks like.

## The built-in template, in your language

The default layout speaks German. `locale` switches the labels, the number format and the date format
in one go:

```ts
const { bytes, xml } = await renderZugferd(invoice, { locale: "en" });
```

Individual labels can be overridden on top of the preset, which is enough for most house styles:

```ts
await renderZugferd(invoice, {
  locale: "en",
  labels: { vat: "Sales Tax", grandTotal: "Amount due" },
});
```

The keys are the parts of the page, and you override only the ones you care about:

`allowance` · `alreadyPaid` · `amount` · `amountDue` · `amountsIn` · `bankDetails` ·
`buyerVatId` · `charge` · `contactPerson` · `contractReference` · `creditNote` ·
`customerReference` · `deliverTo` · `deliveryDate` · `description` · `dueDate` · `email` ·
`grandTotal` · `invoice` · `invoiceDate` · `invoiceNumber` · `itemNumber` · `netTotal` ·
`orderNumber` · `page` · `pageOf` · `payableBy` · `payee` · `payment` · `paymentMeans` ·
`perQuantity` · `phone` · `plusVat` · `position` · `quantity` · `registration` ·
`remittance` · `servicePeriod` · `subtotal` · `taxAmount` · `taxNumber` · `taxableBase` ·
`unitPrice` · `vat` · `vatBreakdown` · `vatId`

`resolveLabels(locale, overrides)` is exported too, if you want the resolved set for a page you build
yourself.

## A layout you designed yourself

Hand `pdf` a `Document` and jasy uses it instead of the built-in one, then embeds the XML, the
attachment, the PDF/A-3 metadata and the color profile around it. Everything that makes the file
conformant is still done for you:

```ts
import { renderZugferd } from "@jasy/e-invoice";
import { Document, Page, Column, Row, Text, Divider, Image } from "@jasy/pdf";

const { bytes, xml } = await renderZugferd(invoice, {
  pdf: Document([
    Page({ size: "A4", margin: 48, gap: 14 }, [
      Row({ justify: "between", align: "center" }, [
        Image("logo.svg", { width: 90 }),
        Text("INVOICE", { size: 26, bold: true, color: "#1450aa" }),
      ]),
      Divider({ color: "#d0d4da" }),
      Column({ gap: 6 }, [
        Text(`No. ${invoice.number}`, { bold: true }),
        Text(`Issued ${invoice.issueDate}`, { color: "gray" }),
      ]),
      // ... your table, your totals, your footer
    ]),
  ]),
});
```

The XML that comes back is **byte-for-byte the same** as with the default template. That is the whole
point of the split: the appearance is a design decision, the XML is a legal one, and changing the
first cannot break the second.

### One thing that stays your responsibility

You are on the hook for one thing the default template does for you: German law (§14 UStG) requires
certain particulars to be **visible on the page**, not merely present in the XML - the seller and
buyer, the invoice number and date, the quantity and kind of goods, the net amount per VAT rate, the
rate itself and the tax amount. Print them, and make sure a long value wraps rather than being cut:
`Text(value, { breakWord: true })`. A truncated mandatory field is a missing one.

### Starting from the built-in one

Both halves of the default are exported, so you rarely have to start from nothing:

```ts
import { defaultInvoiceTemplate, bundledFonts } from "@jasy/e-invoice";
```

`defaultInvoiceTemplate` builds the standard page from an invoice, which is a useful thing to read or
to wrap. `bundledFonts()` returns the **Liberation** families keyed by the standard-14 names they
substitute - `Helvetica`, `Times`, `Courier`. Registering them under those names is what lets a
ZUGFeRD file use familiar font names and still be PDF/A valid, because PDF/A requires every font to be
embedded and the standard 14 are not.

```ts
await renderToBytes(doc, { fonts: await bundledFonts() });
```

## Invoicing periods

An invoice for a recurring service is often about a **period** rather than a delivery date, and §14
UStG accepts either. Both levels are supported and land in the XML as `ram:BillingSpecifiedPeriod`
(CII) or `cac:InvoicePeriod` (UBL):

```ts
const invoice = {
  // ...
  period: { start: "2026-06-01", end: "2026-06-30" }, // the whole document
  lines: [
    {
      name: "Managed hosting",
      period: { start: "2026-06-01", end: "2026-06-30" }, // or per line
      quantity: 1,
      unit: "MON",
      netUnitPrice: 240,
      vat: { category: "S", ratePercent: 19 },
    },
  ],
};
```

The XRechnung rule wants a delivery date, **or** a document period, **or** a period on _every_ line -
and the pre-check enforces exactly that, `every` and not `some`. A period that ends before it starts is
refused too.

## What comes back

`renderZugferd` returns three things, not two:

```ts
const { bytes, xml, droppedCharacters } = await renderZugferd(invoice);
```

`droppedCharacters` holds any character no embedded font could draw. It was **removed** rather than
written as the font's `.notdef` box, because PDF/A forbids referencing that glyph - so the file stays
conforming and the invoice still goes out. It is empty for almost every document. Show it to whoever
created the invoice rather than logging it:

```ts
if (droppedCharacters.length > 0) {
  warnUser(`removed, no font can draw them: ${droppedCharacters.join(" ")}`);
}
```

That is deliberately a return value and not a policy option: a missing tick mark must never stop an
invoice from being produced, but a server log is not a report.

## Working out the totals yourself

`computeInvoice(invoice)` runs the same arithmetic the template and the XML use, and hands it back:
`lineNets` and `lineTotal`, `allowanceTotal` and `chargeTotal`, `taxBasisTotal`, the `vatBreakdown`
per category and rate, `taxTotal`, `grandTotal`, `paidAmount` and `duePayable`. Each `vatBreakdown`
entry carries its `category` and `ratePercent`, the `taxableAmount` it applies to, the `taxAmount`
itself, and an `exemption` reason for the categories that need one. Use it when you draw your own page
and want the numbers to agree with the XML by construction rather than by hand.

Every amount is an exact `Decimal`, not a JavaScript number - `0.1 + 0.2` never turns into a cent off. (changed in beta.3)
`toDecimalString` turns one into text:

```ts
import { computeInvoice, toDecimalString } from "@jasy/e-invoice";

const totals = computeInvoice(invoice);
Text(`Total ${toDecimalString(totals.grandTotal)} EUR`);
```

---

Source: https://jasy.dev/docs/cli
Summary: The jasy CLI reads, validates and exports ZUGFeRD and XRechnung invoices from your terminal - KoSIT rules and veraPDF, and nothing leaves your machine.

# The jasy CLI

`@jasy/cli` turns any ZUGFeRD or XRechnung PDF into something you can read, check and export, right from
your terminal. It runs entirely on your machine. No upload, no account.

## Install

You do not have to install anything. Run it once with `npx`:

```bash
npx @jasy/cli validate ./invoice.pdf
```

If you reach for it often, install it globally and use the `jasy` command everywhere:

```bash
pnpm add -g @jasy/cli
```

The examples below use the `jasy` command. With `npx`, write `npx @jasy/cli` instead.

## Read an invoice

`jasy read` pulls the embedded XML out of the PDF and shows you what the invoice actually says: the
parties, the line items and the totals. It understands both CII (ZUGFeRD) and UBL (PEPPOL).

```bash
jasy read invoice.pdf
```

```text
✓ invoice.pdf  ·  ZUGFeRD · EN 16931 (CII)

  invoice    INV-2026-0042
  date       2026-06-21   due 2026-07-05
  from       Northwind Studio GmbH
  to         Globex Corporation Ltd

  1 C62  Website design & build                      9600.00
  12 HUR  Strategy consulting                        1680.00
  ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
  net 11280.00   VAT 2143.20   total 13423.20 EUR
```

Need the raw XML? Add `--xml` to print it, or `-o invoice.xml` to save it.

```bash
jasy read invoice.pdf --xml
```

## Validate an invoice

`jasy validate` checks the invoice against the real rules: the official EN 16931 business rules, the
German XRechnung (BR-DE) rules when it is an XRechnung, and the structural PDF/A-3 requirements. It
exits non-zero when something is wrong, so it slots straight into a script or CI.

```bash
jasy validate invoice.pdf
```

```text
  invoice.pdf  ·  XRechnung (CII)

  XRechnung rules     ✓ valid
  PDF/A-3 structure   ✓ 13/13
  PDF/A (veraPDF)     n/a - `jasy verapdf --install` for the full ISO check

  → VALID
```

These are the same KoSIT Schematron rules the German authorities use, run locally against your own
file. No upload.

## The full PDF/A check

The structural checks already cover the everyday case. For the complete ISO 19005 (PDF/A) verdict, jasy
can wire up [veraPDF](https://verapdf.org), the official open-source validator. The doctor tells you
what you have and what to do next:

```bash
jasy verapdf
```

```text
  Java        ✓ 21.0.11
  veraPDF     ✗ not found
  → jasy verapdf --install
```

veraPDF is a Java application, so a Java runtime is the one requirement. Install it locally, no admin,
into `~/.jasy/verapdf`:

```bash
jasy verapdf --install
```

Once it is there, `jasy validate` adds a full `PDF/A (veraPDF)` line automatically. It is never a gate.
Your structural checks carry the everyday case on their own.

## Export the data

`jasy export` reads the invoice back into structured data and writes it as JSON, plain text or a
spreadsheet. The format follows the `-o` extension, or the `-f` flag.

```bash
jasy export invoice.pdf -f json          # JSON to stdout
jasy export invoice.pdf -o invoice.xlsx  # an Excel file
```

JSON gives you the full invoice model plus a computed totals block, ready to drop into your own system.

## The interactive terminal

Run `jasy` with no arguments to open the interactive terminal. Press `o` to open an invoice and it
shows the parties, the line items, the totals and every check in one view. From there, `j` / `t` / `x`
export to JSON, text or Excel.

```bash
jasy
```

It is the same engine as the commands above, with a UI around it.
